[]` to build `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId}/events`, i.e. always the first destination. Meanwhile EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now iterates every destination and calls createEvent per credential, and CalendarManager swallows 404s in its catch (returns undefined). So for multi-host collective bookings with O365 hosts, non-first hosts would target the first host's calendar id under their own auth — the described silent-failure mechanism is grounded in the diff. Google's service was updated to filter by credentialId; Office365 (and Lark, though the finding cites O365) were not.

judged_text: Office365CalendarService.createEvent ignores which credential is creating the event and always targets destinationCalendar[0], while EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination. For a collective booking with more than one O365 host, only the first host's calendar receives the event; every other host's call posts to `/me/calendars/{firstHostCalendarId}/events` under their own auth, 404s, and is swallowed by CalendarManager's catch — the other hosts' calendars silently never get the event, so the PR's stated collective multi-host goal only works for Google Calendar.

For a collective booking with more than one O365 host, only the first host's calendar receives the event; every other host's call posts to `/me/calendars/{firstHostCalendarId}/events` under their own auth, 404s, and is swallowed by CalendarManager's catch — the other hosts' calendars silently never get the event, so the PR's stated collective multi-host goal only works for Google Calendar.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent` per destination/credential (passing `destination.externalId` only to `CalendarManager.createEvent`). However `CalendarManager.createEvent` invokes the app service as `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and does not pass the per-destination externalId into the service. In `Office365CalendarService.createEvent`, the target URL is chosen from the *first* destination calendar only (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then `/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId}/events`), so every per-credential call will still attempt to write to destinationCalendar[0] regardless of which credential is used. If the first calendarId doesn’t belong to the current credential, Office365 will likely 404; `CalendarManager.createEvent` explicitly swallows 404s and returns undefined, so other hosts’ events can be silently missing. This matches the finding’s described failure mode for collective multi-host non-Google calendars.
